thread:
Ashley: Heads-up — saw a repeatable perf regression on a new batch of GPUs we got from vendor B. Seqlen 512 requests fall back to the generic matmul kernel and lose ~12% throughput compared to prod baseline. Suspect capability-detection misclassifying tensor-core availability.
Ronan: Ugh. Which field is misreported? SM or a driver quirk? :eyes:
Ashley: The hw signature reports SM92 but the device reports no TF32/tc ops in the microprobe. Our kernel picker says SM>=90 -> tensor-core path, but the runtime double-check fails later and chooses slow path.
Nina: Can you paste the mini repro and perf numbers?
Ashley: Repro on one box (quick):
```
./probe_hw --device 0 --tiny-bench --precision bf16
# outputs
SM: 92
driver: 540.12
tc_supported: false
probe_matmul_latency_us: 85.2
expected_tc_latency_us: 21.3
```
Ronan: That latency delta screams misrouted kernel. Is this deterministic across all batches or only certain seqlen/bs combos?
Ashley: Deterministic for seqlen 512, bs 8+; seqlen 64/128 pick tc path fine. So it's sequence-length-dependent gating in our autotuner.
perf-bot: Regression detected: branch=main, commit=ab12cd3, metric=throughput, delta=-11.9% @ seqlen=512 on SM92 cluster (n=10). See /perf/runs/48912345
Nina: Hmm — our gating heuristic uses estimated shared memory & occupancy thresholds that change sign at seqlen ~256. If the microprobe returned subtle error (timeout) we treat tc_supported=false. Could be flaky microprobe on older drivers.
Ronan: Possible mitigation: add a second-stage microbench (tiny matmul) at runtime just-in-time before shipping kernel choice for first few requests; fallback to generic if it fails repeatedly. That way hardware signature and runtime check agree.
Ashley: Agreed. Suggest a conservative guard: only run JIT microbench when hw signature indicates TC but microprobe says no, and only for seqlen in [256,1024]. Also add telemetry flag so we can retroactively inspect hits.
Kai: Quick patch idea: set env REDWOOD_RUNTIME_HWGUARD=1 to enable. Pseudocode:
```
if (hw.sig >= SM90 && !microprobe.tc_ok) {
  if (seqlen >= 256 && seqlen <= 1024) {
    run_jit_probe(); // 3-5 iterations, timeout 50ms
    if (jit_probe.tc_ok) choose_tc_path(); else choose_generic();
  } else choose_generic();
}
```
Nina: We should be careful about adding extra latency on cold start. JIT probe must be backgrounded or run async on the first request while using conservative kernel. Also we should cache result per-device.
Ashley: Right — cache per device id and TTL 24h. Also include a sampling rate flag to avoid microbenching all devices during rollout.
Ronan: Test plan: 1) roll patch to internal canary pool 2) run perf harness across SM92/86/95 with driver matrix 3) collect telemetry + compare commit ab12cd3 baseline.
perf-bot: Perf harness scheduled: /jobs/48912346 — will run 24h.
Kai: I'll open a quick PR with the flag and the jit_probe hook, add logging key hw.guard.jit_probe_result -> {device_id, seqlen, pass}.
Nina: Also add an exception for FP8-only models — if model quant profile requires fp8 we should prefer path that supports fp8 even if bf16 tc is flaky.
Ashley: Good call. For now, prioritize TC for bf16; FP8 gating will be follow-up.
Ronan: Action items: Kai PR + unit microbench + canary deployment (Kai), telemetry dashboard (Nina), perf run verification (Ashley). ETA EOD tomorrow for PR.
Ashley: Thanks — will watch perf job and paste results. :thumbsup:
